r-cli-update.accept: 'macacfs update' updates all; 'macacfs update br ntm' updates just those; both re-run the tool's install/update method to latest.
r-cli-update.text: macacfs CLI updates tools individually or all together, manually.

r-dry-run.accept: 'macacfs install --dry-run' changes nothing on disk/PATH and runs no network installs; output lists intended actions.
r-dry-run.text: A dry-run mode that performs NO real installs — only prints what it would do.

r-fail-loud.accept: Forcing one tool to fail yields a ❌ line in the summary and a non-zero exit code; failure is not swallowed.
r-fail-loud.text: Fail loud: no silent fallbacks; per-tool failures surfaced with error output in a summary and non-zero exit if any tool failed.

r-github-repo.accept: gh repo view shows a public repo under the user's account; README states the scope plainly.
r-github-repo.text: Published as a PUBLIC GitHub repo via gh CLI, with a simple README framing it as a mini-ACFS-for-Mac doing only its few things.

r-install-all.accept: After 'macacfs install', each tool's CLI (br, ntm, am, ...) resolves on PATH and reports a version.
r-install-all.text: Install all 39 Dicklesworthstone ACFS-suite tools/CLIs on macOS (the full list incl. JFP's CLI).

r-macos-only.accept: Refuses to run on non-darwin with a clear message; no apt/systemctl/useradd calls anywhere.
r-macos-only.text: Runs on macOS only (darwin); does not attempt Ubuntu/systemd/root-VPS machinery.

r-method-dispatch.accept: Manifest row per tool names its method; installing a sample of each method type succeeds on the Mac.
r-method-dispatch.text: Per-tool install/update dispatch across ~5 methods: own install.sh (curl|bash), Homebrew tap, cargo install --git, go install/Makefile, npm/bash.

r-no-servers.accept: No launchctl-load of tool services, no 'am serve', no daemon starts; code shows only build/install/update actions for tools.
r-no-servers.text: Never start/run any servers or long-running services (e.g. mcp_agent_mail). Install and update binaries only.

r-prefer-brew.accept: MS and SRPS rows use the brew method; install/update go through brew for them.
r-prefer-brew.text: Prefer Homebrew where a tool publishes a tap/formula (e.g. MS, SRPS).

r-prereq-autoinstall.accept: On a Mac missing e.g. go, running macacfs installs go before the tools that need it; gate reports what it installed.
r-prereq-autoinstall.text: Prerequisite gate checks for required toolchains (git, curl, Homebrew, rust/cargo, go, uv, node/bun) and INSTALLS any that are missing, not just reports them.

r-retry-escalation.accept: Simulated failure states drive the schedule: fail->nightly; 3 fails->2pm daily; success->back to weekly.
r-retry-escalation.text: If a scheduled run fails, retry the next night nightly until success; after 3 consecutive nightly failures switch to daily 2pm attempts until success, then return to weekly.

r-run-tracking.accept: A state file records last-run timestamp and success/failure; readable after each run.
r-run-tracking.text: The scheduled updater records when it last ran and whether that run succeeded or failed.

r-scope-min.accept: Feature set maps only to those items; none of the ACFS VPS machinery is present.
r-scope-min.text: Minimal scope: install tools, install a weekly-update plist, manual update via CLI, and self-update. Not a full ACFS port (no user provisioning, OS upgrade, service orchestration, phase runner).

r-self-update.accept: 'macacfs self-update' (or --self-update) fetches the repo and replaces the installed macacfs with the latest; version reflects the update.
r-self-update.text: macacfs can update ITSELF via a bootstrap self-update flag (same pattern ACFS uses): re-download the repo and reinstall the macacfs tool from it.

r-weekly-plist.accept: macacfs installs a ~/Library/LaunchAgents plist; launchctl lists it; normal cadence is weekly.
r-weekly-plist.text: Installs a launchd LaunchAgent plist that runs the update weekly.
